# Data Source: tfe_current_user

Get the current user associated with the API token. When authenticated with a team or organization token, HCP Terraform returns a synthetic service user rather than a real user account, so attributes like `email` and `username` will not reflect a real person.

## Example Usage

```python
import constructs as constructs
import cdktf as cdktf
# Provider bindings are generated by running cdktf get.
# See https://cdk.tf/provider-generation for more details.
import ...gen.providers.tfe as tfe
class MyConvertedCode(cdktf.TerraformStack):
    def __init__(self, scope, name):
        super().__init__(scope, name)
        data_tfe_current_user_current =
        tfe.data_tfe_current_user.DataTfeCurrentUser(self, "current")
        cdktf.TerraformOutput(self, "email",
            value=data_tfe_current_user_current.email
        )
```

```python
import constructs as constructs
import cdktf as cdktf
# Provider bindings are generated by running cdktf get.
# See https://cdk.tf/provider-generation for more details.
import ...gen.providers.tfe as tfe
class MyConvertedCode(cdktf.TerraformStack):
    def __init__(self, scope, name):
        super().__init__(scope, name)
        data_tfe_current_user_current =
        tfe.data_tfe_current_user.DataTfeCurrentUser(self, "current")
        tfe.organization_membership.OrganizationMembership(self, "owner",
            email=cdktf.Token.as_string(data_tfe_current_user_current.email),
            organization="my-org"
        )
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `email` (String) The email address of the current user.
- `id` (String) The ID for the user.
- `is_service_account` (Boolean) Whether the current user is a service account.
- `username` (String) The username of the current user.
